Thanks Chloe — that list looks great. Short answer on scope: a statement is acceptable for initial catalog intake, but the pen-test needs to be demonstrably scoped to the services that handle untrusted inputs and the inference path (model-as-a-service endpoints). If the existing letter lists service names/hosts or an architecture diagram tying the tests to the runtime, that's usually sufficient for review.

Two additional asks from the review team:
- Can you provide a small control mapping CSV that maps SOC2/ISO controls -> Redwood control owner + evidence artifact name (headers we ask for: control_id, control_family, redwood_control_name, owner, evidence_file)
- If there are any outstanding high-severity findings in the last 6 months, include a short remediation timeline; low/medium items are ok in the POA&M.

If you can drop the mapping sheet and POA&M into the folder and share the link, the catalog team will start the intake. If anything looks like it might delay co-sell approval by more than 3 business days, flag it and we'll coordinate a risk memo.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Maria
